interpretation.primary_finding: STC-1010 ranks 3rd or 4th in 98.1% of unselected MSS CRC patients. PRIME/PEAK_FOLFIRI (mapk=0.8) dominate because mapk=0.70 is fixed for all MSS patients, and the io axis (STC-1010 primary driver) is suppressed by low TMB in MSS CRC (median TMB=3.3 mut/Mb → io=0.226).
interpretation.enrichment_finding: In TMB ≥ 25 subgroup (n=9, 1.9% of MSS cohort), STC-1010 ranks 1st for all 9 patients. Δ=+0.143, recall@3=1.0, MRR=1.0. This is the expected enrichment signal.
interpretation.clinical_implication: STC-1010 mechanism-fit advantage is confined to the high-TMB MSS subgroup. This aligns with CO.26 pTMB ≥28 OS HR=0.34 — the strongest IO signal in MSS CRC. BreAK CRC-001 GAP-02 (no prospective pTMB collection) is the critical design gap.
interpretation.governance_note: Canonical fit 0.6944 is governance-locked from KG v2 JSON. Per-patient ranker uses canonical_vectors.py vectors (fit=0.6944 for canonical patient). Discrepancy is a known KG v2 transcription error documented in canonical_vectors.py.
interpretation.crossover_finding: STC-1010 beats PRIME at io ≥ 0.44 (TMB ≈ 30 mut/Mb). In this TCGA cohort, no patients fall in TMB 25–50 range — the 9 TMB-hypermutated patients all have TMB 102–382 mut/Mb (io=0.60 cap). The TMB crossover threshold is clinically relevant but not testable in this cohort.
interpretation.hrd_low_finding: HRD-Low patients show higher recall@3 (0.94) than HRD-Intermediate (0.44) or HRD-High (0.38). Mechanism: HRD-Low patients have lower aneuploidy (median=7.0 vs 16.0) → lower efflux → lower N0147 fit (N0147 efflux=0.3 is its primary axis). STC-1010 beats N0147 for 141/150 HRD-Low patients.
